$comment: Backlog for the AMPLS + DNS Private Resolver migration. Types are logical (epic/feature/story/task) and mapped to your process by New-AdoBacklog.ps1. 'template' features are expanded once per entry in 'waves'; 'forEachSubscription' stories once per entry in 'workloadSubscriptions'. Placeholders: {{wave.n}} {{wave.name}} {{wave.zones}} {{wave.forwarders}} {{sub.name}} {{sub.id}}.

waves.name: ACR, App Service and non-blob storage
Blob storage and AMPLS
waves.forwarders: blob.core.windows.net, monitor.azure.com, oms.opinsights.azure.com, ods.opinsights.azure.com, agentsvc.azure-automation.net, applicationinsights.azure.com

epic.title: Centralise Private Link DNS on Azure DNS Private Resolver and AMPLS
description: Move every privatelink.* zone off the enterprise DNS servers into central Azure Private DNS zones in the connectivity subscription.
On-prem DNS keeps only conditional forwarders to the DNS Private Resolver inbound endpoint.
Azure Monitor traffic moves to a single shared AMPLS in the management subscription.
Runbook, scripts and Terraform: repo folder ampls-dns-migration (README run order).
ac: No privatelink.* zones hosted on enterprise DNS servers
All private endpoints register through zone groups in the central zones (DINE policy compliant)
On-prem, spoke and ARO clients resolve PaaS FQDNs to private IPs (scripts 09/test-resolution.sh green)
AMPLS ingestion in PrivateOnly with every workspace/component scoped; no stale agent heartbeats

features.title: Foundation: DNS Private Resolver and central zones (connectivity subscription)
description: Build the resolver, central privatelink zones and links in the connectivity subscription. No client impact.
ac: Resolver inbound IP answers from on-prem and from a spoke
All zones in zone-map.json exist in rg-dns-privatezones with a CanNotDelete lock

stories.title: Deploy DNS Private Resolver in the hub (inbound, outbound, forwarding ruleset)
description: Terraform: infra/terraform/connectivity.tf
Inbound endpoint static IP; ruleset forwards on-prem domains only (no Azure public zones, avoids loops).
ac: dig @<inbound-ip> management.azure.com answers from on-prem
corp domain resolves from a hub VM through the outbound ruleset

CanNotDelete lock on rg-dns-privatezones
